name: Mac Battery
tagline: See your MacBook's battery on your iPhone, iPad, widgets and Apple Watch.
status: TestFlight beta (not on the public App Store yet)
about:
Mac Battery shows your MacBook's battery level live on your iPhone, including the Dynamic Island and Lock Screen, and on your iPad, widgets and Apple Watch. It sends you alerts for things like low battery or charging. The Mac menu-bar app also has a notch panel with CPU load, fans and temperature, free disk space, and what is playing in Music or Spotify.

The app has no accounts. It uses your own iCloud to move data between your devices.

collects.shared: Only you, through your iCloud. The developer cannot read it.
collects.why: To show the battery on your iPhone, iPad, Watch and widgets.

collects.shared: Only you. Your Mac reads it.
collects.why: To show other devices' battery on the Mac and to send low-battery alerts.

collects.why: To update the Live Activity and widgets and to send alerts.

usage_data:
Mac Battery keeps an activity log on each device. It writes a short line every 10 seconds, even when idle. It also records taps and clicks, background jobs, network requests (the address, result and time taken) and errors. Passwords, keys and tokens are masked.

The log stays on the device in files for 30 days, then it is deleted. The folder is capped at about 1 GB. On the Mac the files are in the Logs folder (inside the app's container if the app is sandboxed). iPhone, iPad and Watch also copy their log, in batches of up to 4 MB about every 10 minutes, to your own private iCloud. Your Mac pulls those into its own log folder so you can read everything in one place. The developer's servers do not receive these logs.

You can read the log on the device in a hidden developer screen. A log reaches the developer only if you tap "Send to support", and then only the last few masked lines, after you have seen a preview.
not_collected: No tracking across other companies' apps or websites
No contacts, photos, camera, microphone, health data or location

third_parties.what: Your data lives in your own private iCloud. Apple's push service receives the battery numbers and alert text that your Mac sends to update your Live Activity and widgets.
An encrypted support report, only when you tap Send. The developer holds the key to read it.
Update checks, only in the direct-download Mac version.

permissions.name: Notifications
permissions.why: To alert you about battery events. On iPhone, battery under 5% can use a time-sensitive alert.

permissions.name: iCloud
permissions.why: To sync battery data between your own devices.

permissions.name: Live Activities
permissions.why: To show the battery on the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island.

permissions.name: Background updates (iPhone and iPad)
permissions.why: To receive updates and refresh data when the app is not open.

permissions.name: Automation of Music and Spotify (Mac)
permissions.why: To show what is playing in the notch and let you play, pause and skip.

permissions.name: Screen Recording (Mac, optional, off by default)
permissions.why: Only if you turn on the screen capture and text recognition feature. macOS then asks for Screen Recording so the app can take a picture of the part of the screen you pick.

permissions.name: Launch at login (Mac)
permissions.why: So the menu-bar app is running when you start your Mac.

retention:
Logs are kept for 30 days, then deleted.

To clear this device, open Settings and choose "Erase All Data on This Device" (Mac, iPhone, iPad and Watch). It clears settings, setup, waiting alerts, the Live Activity, the Mac's imported push key and the local logs. It does NOT touch your other devices, the data in your iCloud, or anything on a server. The device ID in the Keychain is kept.

Device records in your iCloud are removed automatically after 30 days without activity. You can also remove the app's iCloud data in your device's iCloud storage settings. Backups and exports are files you control. A support report you already sent cannot be taken back.
children: Mac Battery is not directed at children. It has no accounts and the developer does not collect data from anyone, including children.
support_what: Mac Battery shows how much charge your MacBook has left on your iPhone, iPad, widgets and Apple Watch, and alerts you about low battery or charging. The Mac app lives in the menu bar and also has a notch panel with system information and music controls.
support_steps: Install the Mac app on your MacBook and the iPhone or iPad app on your other devices.
Sign in to the same iCloud account on all of them.
Allow notifications when asked, so you get battery alerts.
Open the app on your iPhone to see your Mac's battery and start the Live Activity.
Add the widget or Watch complication if you want it on your Home Screen or watch face.
If something looks wrong, open the app's Help screen and run the self-checks.

support_faq.q: Does the developer see my battery data?
support_faq.a: No. Battery data moves between your devices through your own private iCloud. The developer cannot read it.

support_faq.q: Can I stop the Live Activity?
support_faq.a: Yes. The app has a Stop Live Activity button on the screen that starts it and in Settings.

support_faq.q: How do I reset the app on one device?
support_faq.a: Go to Settings and choose "Erase All Data on This Device". It does not change your other devices or your iCloud data.

support_faq.q: What does Send to support send?
support_faq.a: It shows you a preview first. If you send it, it includes app and system versions, your device model, network type, Help-chat text, self-check results, an optional note, and a few masked log lines.

support_faq.q: Why does the Mac ask about Music or Spotify?
support_faq.a: The notch panel shows what is playing and has play, pause and skip buttons. That needs your permission to control those apps.
